chunks: Whoever reaches the Day of Tarwiyya (8th of Dhu al-Hijja) at the declining of the sun until night has attained the Hajj al-Tamattu'.
And whoever reaches the Day of al-Nahr (10th of Dhu al-Hijja) at Muzdalifa with five people has attained the Hajj.

key_terms.المتعة: Hajj al-Tamattu', the combined Umra-then-Hajj pilgrimage, one of the three forms of Hajj
key_terms.زوال الشمس: The declining of the sun, i.e., when the sun passes its zenith at noon, marking the time of zuhr prayer
key_terms.مزدلفة: Muzdalifa, the sacred ground between Mina and Arafat where pilgrims spend the night after Arafat
key_terms.يوم التروية: The Day of Tarwiyya, the 8th of Dhu al-Hijja, when pilgrims historically gathered water and headed to Mina
key_terms.يوم النحر: The Day of Sacrifice/al-Nahr, the 10th of Dhu al-Hijja (Eid al-Adha), when animals are slaughtered

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for attaining Hajj al-Tamattu' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes legal rulings on the minimum requirements for attaining two forms of Hajj. A pilgrim who arrives at Mecca by noon on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijja has successfully qualified for Hajj al-Tamattu', while a pilgrim who reaches Muzdalifa on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijja with five companions has fulfilled the Hajj. These rulings are significant for pilgrims who face difficulty completing all the rites on time, as they specify the minimum thresholds recognized in Shia jurisprudence.
